extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: CONTEXTUAL is a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require context-sensitive reasoning for text-rich images. It consists of 506 challenging instructions for Large Multimodal Model (LMM) evaluation, covering eight real-world visual scenarios: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application usage, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes. Each instance contains a human-written instruction (question or imperative task) and a human-written ground-truth response.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng (University of California Los Angeles)
extraction.publisher: PMLR (Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning)
extraction.citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., & Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources including LAION-5B (for Time, Shopping, Navigation, Abstract categories using keyword search via CLIP-retrieval UI), Rico Dataset (for Application Usage), Open WebText Initiative (for Web Usage via website scraping), and test sets of existing VQA datasets InfographicVQA (for Infographic), STVQA and ESTVQA (for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes). After image collection, authors were divided into two groups to annotate instruction-response pairs following guidelines that require context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements. Samples were then verified by MTurk workers and cross-reviewed between author groups.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B, Rico Dataset (66,000 UI screens from 9,300 Android apps), Open WebText Initiative website links, InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Stage 1 filtering: Images for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories underwent manual filtering. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, heuristic-based filtering was applied using PaddleOCR to detect text in images, selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of words for annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation process: Stage 1 involved shortlisting images via manual and heuristic-based filtering. Stage 2 involved authors divided into two groups, each responsible for annotating four specific categories with instruction-response pairs, following guidelines that require context-sensitive reasoning (avoiding OCR-only solvable questions, covering questions and imperative tasks, varied complexity). Stage 3 involved MTurk workers verifying each sample, followed by cross-review between author groups. Final dataset contains 506 instances.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for verification and human performance baseline); authors performed primary annotation manually.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 96% of the samples were annotated correctly as per MTurk verification. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and cross-review between author groups ensured adherence to guidelines and filtered out low-quality samples. Human evaluation used majority vote among three annotators.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One human-written instruction-response pair per item (created by authors). For human evaluation, three human annotators independently rated each of the 1680 predicted responses on 280 instances.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators were sourced primarily from the US via Amazon Mechanical Turk. Authors (from University of California Los Angeles) performed primary annotations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4 model) for text detection in images during filtering; ShareGPT-4V-7B for dense image captions; CLIP-retrieval UI for keyword-based image search.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples (validation set) will be released with reference responses, while the remaining 406 samples will have hidden reference responses. A continuously updated leaderboard is maintained on HuggingFace. Dataset and code are available on the project page (https://con-textual.github.io/).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Authors aimed to ensure images, instructions, and reference responses are not offensive to any social group. No apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information was observed in qualitative analysis.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports real-world applications including assisting the visually impaired in interpreting text-rich scenes (e.g., navigating maps in public spaces) and creative understanding of abstract text-rich images (e.g., memes). Authors acknowledge that existing multimodal models can generate harmful responses despite safeguard filters.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human annotators were mainly from the US, which may affect linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses. This could introduce bias in the human baseline and human evaluation results. Future work could focus on understanding the impact of different social groups on human baseline performance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses is limited by annotator demographics (mainly US-based). Human evaluations are hard to scale and expensive. Creating synthetic data for context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning is challenging. Finding suitable images for joint reasoning is complex, requiring heuristic OCR filtering and manual selection.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case is evaluation/testing/benchmarking of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning tasks. The dataset provides a validation set of 100 samples for model development and a test set of 406 samples with hidden references for benchmark evaluation.
